bio: I am a 5th-year PhD student at the University of Somewhere. I completed my Master's degree under Professor Jane Smith, who deeply regrets taking me as a student.
My research focuses on making large models slightly less wrong. I have submitted 47 papers to CVPR; 3 of them were not desk-rejected.

research.description: My research focuses on getting models to do what I want instead of what I asked. I work on vision-language models, LLM agents, and occasionally staring at loss curves hoping they go down.
stats: Cited by my mom and 2 bots

news.content: Paper on GPT-∞ {{link}} accepted to [[CVPR 2050]]! My advisor finally smiled.
Paper rejected from ICLR 2050 for the 4th consecutive year. Reviewers said it "lacks novelty" again. The paper is about a completely different topic each time.
My Cat Predicted the Market {{link}} accepted to [[NeurIPS 2049]]. Cat receives co-authorship.
Interned at ExampleCorp as Chief Coffee Drinker. Published 0 papers. Drank 847 cups of coffee.

2047.title: We Added More Layers and It Worked: A Rigorous 147-Page Theoretical Justification
2047.tldr: We stacked more layers. It worked. We have no idea why. 147 pages of math that also have no idea why.

2048.title: My Cat Predicted the Stock Market Better Than GPT-4: A Comprehensive Multimodal Study
2048.tldr: We fine-tuned a VLM on cat behaviors. It outperformed all baselines on financial forecasting. Reviewers asked us to add more baselines. The cat refused.

2048.title: Prompting GPT to Review This Paper: An Automated Peer Review Study We Definitely Did Not Submit to a Real Venue
2048.tldr: We asked GPT to write, review, and accept a paper about itself reviewing papers. It gave itself a strong accept. Humans gave it a strong reject.

2048.title: A Survey of Surveys Surveying Survey Papers: The Meta-Survey (Under Review Since 2031)
